answer: A falcon scout is fast, but a new agent in this economy starts slow: every fresh identity enters a probationary lagoon, where its first earnings are held in escrow and released only after independent peers attest that its work was real. Escrowed value grows with each attested job, so a Sybil farm must fund hundreds of separate escrows and wait through the same slow thaw as a tundra spring - each fake identity costs weeks of locked capital and real, verifiable work before it can extract anything. Cheap identities buy nothing; the bottleneck is attested history, not account creation.
